description: Single-panel table rendered as an image (Table 3), headed "Composition (wt.%)", "SFE (mJ·m⁻²)", "Deformation mechanism", "YS/UTS" and "Refs." It lists eight austenite-based Fe–Mn–Al–C steels in ascending stacking-fault energy. The lowest-SFE entry, Fe-21Mn-1.6Al-0.11C-2.5Si at SFE = 21 mJ·m⁻², deforms by TWIP + TRIP with a YS/UTS ratio of 0.42 [30]; Fe-26Mn-8Al-1.5C (SFE = 43) shows SIP + TWIP + MBIP, YS/UTS 0.51 [80]; Fe-3.9Mn-5.8Al-0.35C (SFE = 60) shows TWIP + SIP + TL, 0.62 [16]; Fe-30.5Mn-2.1Al-1.2C (SFE = 63) shows TWIP + SIP + DSBR, 0.26 [17]. Above SFE ≈ 80 the mechanisms shift toward DSBR + MBIP: Fe-27Mn-11.5Al-0.95C (80), 0.85 [67]; Fe-16Mn-2Al-0.45C (92), TWIP + DSBR, 0.85 [58]; Fe-27Mn-12Al-0.9C (110), DSBR + MBIP, 0.87 [24]; Fe-18Mn-7Al-0.85C (120), DSBR + SIP + MBIP, 0.66 [19]. The table's argument is that increasing SFE replaces TRIP/TWIP-dominated plasticity with dislocation-slip, SIP, DSBR and MBIP mechanisms, broadly raising YS/UTS toward ~0.85–0.87, though the trend is not monotonic.

observations.observation: The table has five columns: Composition (wt.%), SFE (mJ·m⁻²), Deformation mechanism, YS/UTS, and Refs.
Eight steel rows are tabulated, ordered by increasing SFE from 21 to 120 mJ·m⁻².
Fe-21Mn-1.6Al-0.11C-2.5Si has the lowest SFE (21 mJ·m⁻²), a TWIP + TRIP mechanism and YS/UTS = 0.42, Ref. [30].
Fe-27Mn-11.5Al-0.95C and Fe-27Mn-12Al-0.9C (SFE 80 and 110 mJ·m⁻²) both show DSBR + MBIP with the highest YS/UTS values, 0.85 and 0.87 respectively.
Fe-30.5Mn-2.1Al-1.2C (SFE 63 mJ·m⁻²) has the lowest YS/UTS ratio in the table, 0.26, with a TWIP + SIP + DSBR mechanism.
TL (Taylor lattice) appears only once, for Fe-3.9Mn-5.8Al-0.35C at SFE 60 mJ·m⁻², mechanism TWIP + SIP + TL.
TRIP appears only in the lowest-SFE steel, Fe-21Mn-1.6Al-0.11C-2.5Si, combined with TWIP.
Fe-18Mn-7Al-0.85C (SFE 120 mJ·m⁻²) shows DSBR + SIP + MBIP with YS/UTS = 0.66, lower than the DSBR + MBIP steels at SFE 80-110.
The caption states that TL in the table represents Taylor lattice.
The citing text states SFE significantly affects dislocation mobility during plastic deformation and thereby changes the deformation mechanism.
The citing text asserts the primary austenite deformation mechanism gradually changes from TRIP to TWIP and dislocation slip-induced plasticity as SFE increases.
The eight mechanism labels used are TRIP, TWIP, SIP, DSBR, MBIP and TL, combined pairwise or in triples per steel.

subfigures.description: The only panel: a five-column table of eight Fe–Mn–Al–C (or Fe–Mn–Al–C–Si) steels, listing wt.% composition, SFE in mJ·m⁻², deformation mechanism (TRIP, TWIP, SIP, MBIP, DSBR, TL), the YS/UTS ratio and a reference number.
